prompt.context: Our client is a German television broadcasting company. It has rights for broadcasting the Champions League Soccer Tournament in Germany. We have been asked to decide whether to broadcast it on the pay-TV channel owned by the client or on the free channel also owned by the client.
prompt.question: Should our client broadcast the Champions League games on its free-TV channel or its pay-TV channel? Please quantify the financial impact of each option.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue sources for each option?
clarifying_info.a: For free TV the revenue comes from advertising. For pay TV the revenue comes from additional subscribers.

clarifying_info.q: How many games would we broadcast, and which teams are involved?
clarifying_info.a: There are 3 German teams, each in a different group in the first round. We only broadcast games with German team participation. In round 1 there are 4 groups of 4 teams; each team plays every other team in its group. In the second round (quarterfinals) there are home and guest games. Then semifinals, then one final. You can assume all German teams advance through every round.
30 seconds of ads cost $50K at any stage of the tournament. A game has 25 minutes of ads.

clarifying_info.q: What ad revenue do we earn if we do NOT broadcast on free TV?
clarifying_info.a: If we decide not to broadcast on free TV we still get the same minutes of advertising at $20K per minute.

clarifying_info.q: What is the pay-TV subscriber impact?
clarifying_info.a: If we broadcast on pay TV we will get 1 million more subscribers. No customers will leave if we decide not to broadcast on pay TV.

clarifying_info.q: What are the pay-TV subscription economics?
clarifying_info.a: Subscription fee (one-time) is $10. Monthly price is $5.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost to acquire and serve pay-TV subscribers?
clarifying_info.a: Acquisition cost is $5 per new customer. It costs $6 per year to serve one customer.

framework: Define the decision: free TV (ad revenue) vs. pay TV (subscriber revenue), evaluated on incremental profit
Count total games broadcast (using tournament structure and 3 German teams advancing)
Calculate incremental ad revenue for free TV (full ad rate minus opportunity cost of alternative programming)
Calculate incremental subscriber revenue and net profit for pay TV (subscription fees minus acquisition and service costs)
Compare incremental profits and recommend the higher-value option
Consider qualitative factors: brand positioning, long-term subscriber base, viewer loyalty

questions.prompt: How many total games will the client broadcast?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build up the tournament structure round by round. Round 1: 3 German teams, each plays 3 games in their group = 9 games. Round 2 (quarterfinals): 3 teams × 2 games (home + away) = 6 games. Round 3 (semifinals): 2 games per team × but teams may share games — casebook counts 4 games. Final: 1 game. Casebook answer is 31 total.

math.setup: R1: each of 3 German teams plays 3 group-stage games = 3×3=9. R2: 3 teams × 2 games (home+guest) = 6. But actually the casebook states R2=8 games and R3=4 games, likely counting all German-involved bracket games. Final = 1. Total = 18+8+4+1 = 31.
steps: Round 1: 3 teams × 6 group games each but only games with German participation; casebook gives 18 games

questions.prompt: What is the incremental ad revenue per game and total incremental revenue for the free-TV option?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize the opportunity cost: without broadcasting the game the client still earns $20K/min in ad revenue, so only the incremental uplift counts. Full rate: 25 min × 2 × $50K = $2.5M per game. Opportunity cost: 25 min × $20K = $500K per game. Incremental = $2.5M − $500K = $2M per game. Total = 31 × $2M = $62M. No additional costs.

math.setup: Ad revenue per game at full rate = 25 min × (2 × $50K/30s) = 25 × $100K = $2.5M. Opportunity cost per game = 25 min × $20K = $0.5M. Incremental revenue per game = $2.5M − $0.5M = $2.0M.
steps: Full ad revenue per game: 25 min × 2 spots/min × $50K/spot = $2.5M
No additional costs for free TV

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit for the pay-TV option?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate total subscription revenue from 1M new subscribers (one-time fee + 12 months), then subtract acquisition and annual service costs. Revenue: 1M × ($10 + $5×12) = 1M × $70 = $70M. Costs: 1M × ($5 + $6) = $11M. Incremental profit = $70M − $11M = $59M.

math.setup: 1M new subscribers. Revenue per subscriber = $10 sign-up fee + $5 × 12 months = $70. Total revenue = 1M × $70 = $70M. Cost per subscriber = $5 acquisition + $6 annual service = $11. Total cost = 1M × $11 = $11M.

questions.guidance: Free TV yields $62M vs. pay TV $59M. The client should broadcast on free TV. Candidate should also flag qualitative considerations such as audience reach, advertiser relationships, long-term subscriber base growth, and competitive dynamics.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the base-case financials, what other factors should the client consider when making this decision?

categories.name: Revenue upside / downside risks
ideas: Ad rates may be higher during high-viewership tournament matches
Subscriber churn after the tournament ends could erode pay-TV gains
Ratings-dependent ad pricing (CPM uplift for live sports)

categories.name: Cost considerations
ideas: Marketing spend to promote pay-TV subscription drive
Technology/infrastructure costs for increased streaming capacity
Potential rights re-negotiation costs if tournament extends

categories.name: Strategic / competitive
ideas: Building pay-TV subscriber base creates long-term recurring revenue
Free TV maximizes reach and brand association with top sports content
Competitor response if they acquire rights for future tournaments
Exclusivity impact on free-TV advertiser relationships

categories.name: Viewer and market dynamics
ideas: German team performance uncertainty (though assumed to advance)
Viewer preference for free vs. paid access to national team games
Potential political/regulatory pressure to keep national sports on free TV

recommendation: Broadcast Champions League games on the free-TV channel
Free TV generates $62M in incremental profit vs. $59M for pay TV — a $3M advantage
Free TV also carries no downside risk from subscriber churn post-tournament
risks: If German teams exit early actual game count drops significantly, reducing free-TV ad revenue
Pay TV could be superior if subscriber retention beyond year 1 is factored in
Ad rates assumed constant; live sports premiums could widen the free-TV advantage further
next_steps: Model multi-year subscriber retention to reassess pay-TV value over a longer horizon
Negotiate higher CPM rates with advertisers given Champions League viewership premiums
Evaluate whether a hybrid simulcast (pay-TV for premium features, free-TV for base broadcast) is permitted under the rights agreement
